newsitem.title: USA: Western gets 47.6 percent of K.C. Power shares, extends deadline.
newsitem.headline: Western gets 47.6 percent of K.C. Power shares, extends deadline.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. said Monday it extended the deadline in its proposed $1.9 billion takeover of Kansas City Power & Light Co., after receiving 47.6 percent of the utility's outstanding shares by the previous deadline.
Western said 29.5 million common shares, or 47.6 million of those outstanding, had been tendered as of the previous deadline last Friday.
Western extended the hostile offer for the Kansas City, Mo.-based company, which is worth $31 a share, to this Friday.
Merger discussions between the two utilities continue, Topeka, Kan.-based Western said.
Lack of shareholder support forced Kansas City Power to abandon its friendly merger agreement with UtiliCorp United Inc. after Western made a rival tender offer.
Western, with assets of more than $6 billion, is a holding company for natural gas and electric utilities.
Kansas City Power's stock rose 25 cents to $28, while Western was unchanged at $30 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
